correctness.rationale: The entire-family crossing obstruction follows from mutually exclusive positivity/negativity intervals for the exact switching normals 1-y and a+y. Both affine half-plane systems are saddles. At a=-5/4,d=-7/4 exact explicit solutions give left and right upper-to-lower flight times 6log(phi) and 4log(phi) with strictly correct half-plane location; both contact normals are opposed. The Filippov tangent field equals (6y²-5y-2)/(9-8y); sign analysis yields exactly one globally attracting root on y<1. The standalone SymPy checker validates each nonstandard identity; its finite interior samples are only diagnostics. Tangencies and sliding cycles are outside the no-crossing scope.

originality.rationale: The origin article matches polynomial first integrals and claims that its exact two-saddle affine example realizes a crossing limit cycle, but the interface-normal signs show one-way crossings for all parameters. Its algebraic closed loop is traversed from upper to lower contact on both sides and is not a positive-time Filippov cycle. The 2021 two-Hamiltonian-saddles nonexistence theorem excludes a different (trace-zero on both sides) class, while the 2024 nilpotent-center/saddle study addresses different half-plane dynamics. Scientific overlap was checked by implication, with publication-priority residual risk.
residual_risks: Some highly relevant historical full texts and any unpublished corrections were not exhaustively inspected; priority is provisional.
The 2023 model may have later author-supplied errata or a nonstandard orbit convention not visible in the consulted publication; the article itself explicitly states the Filippov convention.
No independent mathematical reviewer has assessed these conclusions.

value.rationale: The source presents an exact matched algebraic loop as a limit cycle and uses it to demonstrate sharpness of an upper bound. The new one-way barrier shows that no true crossing cycle exists anywhere in that particular two-parameter family and identifies the source of the geometric/dynamical mismatch. Exact competing flight times and an attracting Filippov pseudoequilibrium diagnose the alternative fate of its benchmark arcs. Such a structural counterexample is pertinent to correct existence proofs for nonsmooth polynomially integrable systems and is not a trivial numerical recomputation.
